text: My name is right there on the front, in gold letters, big gold letters, and you can see it from three blocks away.
People come from all over the world just to take a picture of it. And I tell them, go ahead, take the picture.
Take two. It's the most beautiful building in the city, and everybody knows it. And inside, the lobby, the waterfall, the beautiful pink marble.
Ahh, thank goodness. I hit the ball, and it's going right for the water. Right for the lake. And everybody's watching.
And it bounces once, bounces twice, and it stops, right on the edge. Right on the very edge of the water.
Half an inch! I thought, that's it, it's gone. My heart stopped. But it stayed. It stayed right there. I walked over, and I just looked at it, and I said, thank you.
Thank you, little ball. I was so relieved, I think I let out the biggest breath of my whole life.
The caddie was laughing, I was laughing, everybody was so relieved. I've never been so happy to see a little white ball in my life.
A man came up to me the other day, big strong guy, a builder, hands like this. And he had tears in his eyes.
And he said, sir, the old golf course where I learned to play with my father, they closed it. They're tearing it down.
And I said, that's very sad. That's a very sad thing. Because that's where memories live, you know? Places like that.
You walk on the grass and you remember. And now it's going to be a parking lot. Just a parking lot.
I think about that man sometimes. I really do. We lose a lot of beautiful places like that. And once they're gone, they're gone forever.

I have to admit something, and it's not easy for me. I don't admit things very often. Last week, I was playing golf with my caddie, a young guy, very nice, and I told him, I'm going to beat you by ten strokes.
Ten! And I lost. I lost to the caddie. By four strokes. And everybody at the club heard about it.
Everybody. I walked into the dining room and it got very quiet. Very quiet. People were looking down at their soup.
I'll be honest with you, I was embarrassed. But I'll get him next time. I gave him a very big tip, though.
Whoa! What is this? What's going on here? I walk into the room, the lights are off, and all of a sudden, everybody jumps out!
Surprise! I had no idea. No idea! Look at this cake. This is the biggest cake I've ever seen. It's got my face on it!
Who made this? This is incredible. I've never been so surprised in my life, and I've been surprised a lot, believe me.
You people, you really got me. You got me good. I thought I was coming in for a meeting about the budget!
Listen to me. Listen very carefully. Because I'm only going to say this once. This is the greatest deal. In the history of deals.
Maybe ever. Nobody has seen anything like it. Nobody. And when people look back on this day, many years from now, they're going to say, that was the day.
That was the day everything changed. Remember where you were. Remember who you were with. Because this is history, folks.
Write it down. Tell your children. Tell your grandchildren. They will ask. This is the day. The greatest day. Believe me, folks.
Let me explain how a deal works, because a lot of people don't understand it. First, you never want to look like you need the deal.

Never. Second, you aim very high, and then you keep pushing. Third, you always have a way out. Always. And fourth, and this is the most important one, you have to know the other side better than they know themselves.
That's it. That's the whole thing. It's very simple, but very few people can do it. Very few. Most people give up too soon.
We have the best buildings, the best golf courses, the best hotels, the best restaurants, the best steaks, the best everything.
And people say, how do you do it? How do you do it all? And I say, it's easy, you hire the best people, you work harder than everybody else, and you never, ever give up.
I get up early, I make my calls, I have my meetings, I go to the construction site, I check the marble, I check the windows, I check everything.
Then I have lunch, a quick lunch, and I do it all again. More calls, more meetings, more deals. Every single day.
Okay, okay, we have a lot to cover, so let's go, let's go. Hotels, doing great. Golf courses, doing great, record numbers.
Restaurants, fantastic, people are lining up around the block. The new tower, ahead of schedule, under budget, nobody's ever done that.
The ratings, through the roof, bigger than ever. The steaks, the best steaks, everybody's talking about them. The water, beautiful water, crystal clear.

The vodka, well, we don't talk about the vodka. But everything else, winning, winning, winning. I could go on for hours, I really could, but they tell me we only have a few minutes, so I'm going fast, very fast, faster than anybody's ever gone.
Is that fast enough? I think that's fast enough. Nobody talks faster than me, believe me. Nobody. Oh, and the golf, record rounds, beautiful rounds, the best rounds.
The ties, beautiful ties, very long ties. The hats, everybody wants the hats. The books, bestsellers, all of them, every single one.
Let me tell you something, and I want you to listen. There are people out there, competitors, who think they can beat us.
They think they can take what we built. Let me be very clear. That's not going to happen. Not today, not tomorrow, not ever.
We know who they are. We know what they're doing. And when the time comes, we will be ready. We are always ready.
So to those people, I have a very simple message. Don't even try. You'll lose. You'll lose big. And we will win.
So this guy comes up to me, a little guy, very nervous, and he goes, oh, Mister Trump, Mister Trump, please, please, can I have a picture?
Can I have a picture with you? And I said, sure, of course. And he says, oh, thank you, thank you so much, my wife is never going to believe this!
Oh my goodness! And his voice was going higher and higher, like this, oh, Mister Trump, you're my hero! I thought he was going to faint.
Very nice guy. Very nice. But a very high voice. Later I found out he sings opera. Soprano. Makes sense, actually.
And I said to them, you want the best? You want the very best? Then you came to the right place!
Because we don't do small, we don't do average, we do tremendous! We do spectacular! When we build something, the whole world stops and looks.
They say, how did they do that? How is that possible? And I tell them, it's possible because we dream big, we work hard, and we never, ever quit!
Never! So get ready, folks, because what's coming next is going to be the biggest, the best, the most beautiful thing you've ever seen!
Okay. They gave me this paper, and they said I have to read it, so I'm going to read it.
The terms and conditions of the golf club membership. Section one. Members must wear collared shirts at all times. Section two.
Members must replace all divots on the fairway. Section three. Carts must remain on the cart path near the greens.
Section four. No outside food or beverages. Okay. Very exciting stuff. Section five. Guests must be accompanied by a member.
That's it. That's the paper. I read it. Can I go now? Section six. No running on the greens. Section seven.

Ladies and gentlemen, the moment you've all been waiting for. The winner of this year's club championship, the best golfer at this club, the man with the most beautiful swing anybody has ever seen, is me!
That's right. Me again. And I want to thank the committee, a very fair committee, very honest people. Some of them work for me, but they're very fair.
And I want to thank my caddie, who I beat this time. Not last time. This time. Thank you all very much.
It's been a great year, a great year for golf, and a great year for me. Thank you. Thank you so much.
So they asked me, very serious interview, they said, sir, is it true that you're the greatest golfer in the history of this club?
Yes. Next question. They said, sir, is it true that you've never lost a match? Next question. Then they said, sir, is it true you lost to your caddie last week?
I don't know where you get your information. Very bad information. Terrible sources. Okay, it's true. But he's a very good caddie.
One of the best. Next question, please. Then they said, sir, will you ever play your caddie again? Absolutely not.
Oh, give me a burger, a beautiful burger, with ketchup and pickles and cheese. A tremendous burger, the greatest burger, as golden as golden can be.
